practices.practice: Always validate and sanitize user inputs
practices.description: All user-supplied data must be validated against a whitelist or strict pattern.
practices.remediation: Implement input validation using parameterized queries and prepared statements.

practices.description: Always encode output according to the context in which it will be used (HTML, JavaScript, URL, CSS, etc.)
practices.remediation: Use context-appropriate encoding functions for all dynamic output.

practices.description: Use strong password policies, multi-factor authentication, and secure session management.
practices.remediation: Implement MFA, use strong password policies, secure session tokens.

practices.description: Verify that users have proper authorization before granting access to resources.
practices.remediation: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) and check permissions before all operations.

practices.description: Use well-vetted cryptographic algorithms and avoid hard-coded keys.
practices.remediation: Use AES-256 for encryption, TLS 1.2+ for transport, rotate keys regularly.

practices.description: Do not expose sensitive information in error messages.
practices.remediation: Log detailed errors internally, show generic messages to users.

practices.description: Regularly audit and update all third-party components and libraries.
practices.remediation: Use dependency scanning tools, update regularly, monitor security advisories.

practices.description: Log all security-relevant events without exposing sensitive data.
practices.remediation: Log authentication attempts, access control decisions, security events.

practices.description: Restrict file upload types, size, and location.
practices.remediation: Whitelist allowed file types, store uploads outside webroot, validate MIME types.

practices.description: Use authentication, rate limiting, and input validation for all API endpoints.
practices.remediation: Implement API authentication, rate limiting, CORS policies, input validation.
